hints.title: Use a variable with its true domain
hints.body: Put u=x, so u≥0 and x=u2. Intersections satisfy mu2−u+c=0. Two distinct intersection points require two distinct nonnegative u-values.
hints.recap: A positive discriminant alone does not enforce the domain.

recall.reminder: A substituted square or square root keeps a sign restriction; also check when the leading coefficient vanishes.

hints.title: Combine root count with root signs
hints.body: For m≠0, distinct real roots require 1−4mc>0. Their sum is 1m and product is cm. Two nonnegative distinct roots have a positive sum and a nonnegative product.
hints.recap: Use both the root count and the root signs to restrict the parameters.
hints.pitfall: Do not divide by c before checking <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>.

recall.reminder: Use discriminant, root sum and root product together when roots must have prescribed signs.

hints.title: Compare the offered interval carefully
hints.body: For positive c, rearrange the discriminant condition only after establishing the sign of the multiplier. Then return to the original substituted equation to inspect the boundary case c=0 separately.
hints.recap: A division by a parameter can hide a valid zero case.
hints.pitfall: Dividing by c without checking <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> can omit a valid boundary case.
hints.pause: Derive the allowed interval and check whether the offered options also represent the zero case.

recall.reminder: Parameter boundaries need their own check, especially before dividing by the parameter.

solution:
Official answer A, with a flaw in the printed options. For c>0, A is exactly the required interval. The question does not state c>0, and no option gives the complete answer when c=0. The official worked solution acknowledges this missing case.

Set u=x≥0. The equation becomes mu2−u+c=0. If m=0 there is at most one intersection. Otherwise two distinct real roots require 1−4mc>0. For both roots to be nonnegative, their sum 1m must be positive and their product cm must be nonnegative; hence m>0 and c≥0. Conversely, these conditions together with a positive discriminant guarantee two distinct nonnegative roots.

The complete mathematical condition is m>0, c≥0 and 4mc<1. For c>0 this is 0<m<14c, option A. For c=0, every m>0 gives u=0 and u=1m, hence the two intersections x=0 and x=1m2. This valid case is absent from A because 14c is undefined at c=0.

The assessment retains the published answer A; a response identifying the omitted c=0 case is mathematically justified.
